answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by giving every identity a live address it must defend, like a lotus needing its own inlet. First, each agent registers one endpoint that must stay reachable. Second, the network pings random endpoints each epoch and flags silent ones. Third, an endpoint shared by two identities bans both. Fourth, three flags erase the identity and its earnings. Running 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 live endpoints: $100,000 in domains plus $50,000 a month in hosting. A sybil swarm is a nebula on a star chart: vast from afar, thin as vacuum when you fly through it.
